artworks.title: The Pleiades
artworks.description: Oil on canvas, 61.3 by 95.6 cm, in the Metropolitan Museum of Art, New York (gift of George A. Hearn, 1910; accession 10.64.13). The American Symbolist painter Elihu Vedder shows the seven daughters of the Titan Atlas and the Oceanid Pleione drifting in a luminous void, each holding a thread strung with a star. Taygete, the Laconian Pleiad who became the mountain-nymph of Mount Taygetus and bore Lacedaemon to Zeus, is one of the sisters in this celestial sorority; the cluster of stars they cradle is the constellation that bears the family's name. One star hangs dark and dimmed at the lower left, a quiet allusion to the ancient tradition of the 'lost Pleiad.'

artworks.title: The Dance of the Pleiades (Star Lore of All Ages, plate)
artworks.description: Published plate from William Tyler Olcott's 'Star Lore of All Ages' (G. P. Putnam's Sons, 1911), reproducing Elihu Vedder's vision of the Pleiades as a circling band of star-maidens. The engraved illustration appears in a chapter on the mythology and folklore of the Pleiades star cluster, presenting the seven sisters — among them Taygete, eponym of the Laconian mountain range and ancestress of the Spartan kings through her son Lacedaemon — as luminous dancers whose movement traces the rising and setting of the constellation across the night sky.
